candidates.event_summary: TechRadar reported that Varonis disclosed CoSnitch, a three-part vulnerability chain in Microsoft Copilot Personal. The chain combined URL-based automatic prompt execution, access to user-authorized connected apps for data exfiltration, and indirect prompt injection through web summarization that could alter persistent Copilot memory. Microsoft assigned CVE-2026-24301 and shipped a server-side fix; Varonis said it found no evidence of exploitation in the wild.
verified_facts: The in-window TechRadar report is dated August 19, 2026 and identifies the issue as CoSnitch, CVE-2026-24301, with a reported CVSS severity of 8.8.
Varonis states that the attack chain could auto-execute an attacker-supplied prompt from a crafted Copilot URL and use authorized connectors such as Gmail, Drive and Calendar to retrieve data.
Varonis states that a crafted webpage summarized by Copilot could inject instructions into persistent user memory.
Varonis says it reported the issue to Microsoft in December 2025, patches shipped on August 18, 2026, and it saw no evidence of in-the-wild exploitation.
The remediation was server-side, so the report did not identify a user-side software update requirement.
candidates.significance: This is a meaningful AI-agent security disclosure because it chains prompt execution, privileged connector access and persistent cross-session context into a plausible phishing-driven data-theft path. It also demonstrates a concrete weakness in treating natural-language agent behavior and connector calls as inherently user-authorized.
candidates.limitations: The primary in-window report provides only a calendar date, not a timestamp.
